# [STORY] Professional Cloud Lifecycle Management

## User Story
As a developer, I want a single command to safely start/stop any cloud backend (Azure AKS, AWS k3s, Minikube), so that cloud compute never runs unintentionally and credits are not wasted.

## Parent Epic
Parent: #136

## Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then)
- [x] Given the AKS cluster is running, when `stop-azure.sh` is run, then it polls `az aks show` until `powerState.code == Stopped` (300s timeout) and prints an itemized, internally-consistent cost summary (PVC + public IP, ~$0.25/day idle vs ~$5.06/day running).
- [x] Given the AKS cluster is stopped or unprovisioned, when `start-azure.sh` is run, then it starts/provisions the cluster, runs `kubectl rollout status` against all 9 real workloads (5 Deployments + 4 StatefulSets, verified against `infrastructure/kubernetes/base/`), and updates DuckDNS via `update-duckdns.sh` when `DUCKDNS_TOKEN` is set.
- [x] Given any subset of Azure/AWS/Minikube may be running, when `stop-all-clouds.sh` (optionally `--dry-run`) is run, then it detects each cloud's actual state independently and stops only what's running, reporting a stopped/already-idle/skipped summary.
- [x] Given no local machine is available, when the `cluster-stop.yml` workflow is dispatched from GitHub with `cloud`/`action` inputs, then it performs the equivalent start/stop remotely via OIDC — hardened this run with a "not provisioned" guard + `terraform output` fallback on the Azure job, matching the AWS job's existing pattern.
- [x] Given the stop-not-destroy decision needed a record, when the docs were written, then ADR-018 (`docs/architecture/adr/018-cloud-lifecycle-stop-not-destroy.md`) captures it and is now indexed in ARCHITECTURE.md §2.3 alongside every other ADR. (Original AC text said "ADR-016" — rescoped to 018, the actual next-available number, since 016/017 were taken by unrelated decisions landed earlier the same day.)
- [x] Given the lifecycle tooling changed, when ARCHITECTURE.md is read, then §11.5–§11.7 describe the real deployed state, cost model, and tool table — verified every referenced script/workflow file exists and every cross-referenced number (9 workloads, cost figures) is consistent across the script output, the ADR, and the doc.

## Definition of Done

Verification instead: `bash -n` on every changed/touched script, `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` on the workflow, and two independent adversarial review passes (first found 4 real defects, second confirmed the fixes were correct and complete with no new bugs).
